egress.terms: Downloads are metered against the block's volume (10Gb trial, 20Gb to 6000Gb paid blocks); the Bulk plans have unlimited download size at a capped speed.

record.tooling: Plain NNTP (port 563 SSL), works with any newsreader or an NNTP library.
record.chaining: Trial-shaped and single-use: 10 GB once per account, and Usenet accounts are tied to a paid order flow. Not repeatable at scale.

limits.value: unverified: the plans page states no article or object size limit

Block plans meter download volume: 10Gb trial, then 20Gb to 6000Gb blocks (EUR 5,00 to EUR 140,00); all blocks 30 connections. Bulk plans have unlimited download size at capped speed (Bulk 5: 20 Mbit, 10 connections) up to Bulk Unlimited (unlimited speed, 40 connections).

record.limits_note: Per-object-cap: standard Usenet article size (~750 KB-1 MB practical). Request-rate: 30 connections. Retention: 10 GB is a download volume block, not a storage quota. There is no storage at all here, it is a retrieval service.
record.reliability_note: This is a download-block trial, not free storage: you get 10 GB of retrieval, not 10 GB you can park data in permanently. Categorically the wrong shape for the workload.
